title: Space practice and mix in old items
statement: Revisit each skill at growing intervals on a schedule and mix earlier skills into later practice, so learners must tell which skill an item calls for.
detail: A pedagogy framework behind one project's evaluators makes spaced practice a step on its path to mastery, revisiting key skills 'after a day, a few days, a week, and beyond', and lists cumulative reinforcement among the attributes of a good question: later questions revisit earlier concepts 'to test retention and fluency' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/Incept Pedagogy & Learning Science Overview.md`). It was adopted without a measurement in the project. Mixed, spaced practice checks what was kept, not only first success.
against: The effect is unmeasured here: there was no outside test result for the cohort (0 of 313), so no growth is claimed (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/FACTS_SHEET.md`).

evidence.quote: Students revisit key skills at increasing intervals \- after a day, a few days, a week, and beyond.
Later questions intentionally revisit earlier concepts to test retention and fluency.
so the student must *discriminate* schemas, not pattern-match one per lesson
Spaced review is a single static pass, not a schedule (#11).
kb-0027 names this as cramming, not distributed practice
Distribute practice over time. Cramming creates temporary performance.
Mix problem types to prevent context-dependency.
MAP Science at G7 tests all four MS NGSS domains back-to-back without warning.
The child identifies which procedure to use AND completes all the steps independently.
